line: Anything good planned for the weekend?
followUps: What are you most looking forward to about it?
Is that a regular thing for you, or a one-off?
shareBack: Mention one small plan of your own in a sentence, then ask something else about theirs.

line: This week has flown by. I can't tell yet if that's a good sign.
followUps: Has yours been more busy or more interesting?
What took up most of it?
shareBack: Offer the one thing that ate your week, briefly, then ask what they have left before Friday.
deliveryCue: Say it lightly, as a remark, and leave a pause.

line: What's been the best part of your week so far?
followUps: What made that one stand out?
Is there more of that coming up?
shareBack: Offer your own best moment of the week in one sentence, then hand it back with a question.

line: I'm still working out where to eat around here. Have you found anywhere good for lunch?
followUps: What do you usually order there?
Is it quick enough for a workday?
shareBack: Mention one place you've tried and what you thought, then ask if they know it.

line: While we wait for the others: where are you joining from today?
followUps: Is that your usual spot for calls?
What's it like there today?
shareBack: Say where you are and one detail about it, such as the view or the noise, then ask about theirs.
deliveryCue: Use in the first minute, before the call fills up.

line: Have you watched or read anything good lately? I need something new.
followUps: What did you like about it?
How did you come across it?
shareBack: Name one thing you enjoyed recently and why, in a sentence, then ask if it sounds like their kind of thing.

line: That last session gave me a lot to think about. What did you make of it?
followUps: Which part will you actually use?
Did anything in it surprise you?
shareBack: Offer the one point that stuck with you, then ask whether they saw it the same way.

line: Which session are you most looking forward to today?
followUps: What are you hoping to get out of it?
Have you heard that speaker before?
shareBack: Say which session you picked and why, briefly, then ask what else is on their list.

line: This place was a good pick. Have you been here before?
followUps: What would you recommend?
What's your usual kind of place for a night out?
shareBack: Mention a place you like for evenings like this, in a sentence, then ask if they know it.

line: I can't decide what to order. Does anything look good to you?
followUps: Are you an order-the-same-thing person or do you try new things?
What's the best thing you've eaten lately?
shareBack: Say what you're leaning towards and why, then ask what they'd pick between your two options.

line: Do you have any time off coming up?
followUps: What's the plan for it?
Are you a plan-everything person or a see-what-happens person?
shareBack: Mention your next break, or the one you wish you had, in a sentence, then ask for a tip.

line: Before we start: anything fun on your calendar this week, outside of meetings?
followUps: How did that come about?
Is that something you do often?
shareBack: Offer one thing you have on this week that isn't work, then ask a follow-up about theirs.
deliveryCue: Good for the minute or two before the agenda starts.

line: How was the trip in? Did you have far to come?
followUps: How do you usually pass the time on that trip?
Are you heading straight back afterwards or staying a while?
shareBack: Say how your own trip in went, in a sentence, then ask about the rest of their day.

line: Do you have a go-to coffee order, or do you change it up?
followUps: Where's the best one you've had around here?
Is that a morning-only thing or all day?
shareBack: Admit your own order, however plain, then ask where they'd send you for a good one.

line: I think we're the first ones on. Nice to have a minute before it gets going.
followUps: Has today been back-to-back calls for you?
Anything good planned once you log off?
shareBack: Mention how your day has gone in a few words, then ask what's left on theirs.
deliveryCue: Say it as a remark and let them pick it up.

line: Settle something for me: what's the best snack in the office kitchen?
followUps: What's the one that should never be restocked?
Do you bring lunch in or go out for it?
shareBack: Give your own pick and defend it in a sentence, then ask what they'd add to the shelf.
deliveryCue: Keep it playful.

line: I tried cooking something new at the weekend and it mostly worked. Do you have a dish you always fall back on?
followUps: Who taught you that one?
What's the trick to getting it right?
shareBack: Add one detail about what went wrong with yours, then ask what they'd cook for guests.

line: What's keeping your team busy at the moment?
followUps: Which part of that are you enjoying?
When does it ease off?
shareBack: Name the one thing taking most of your own time, in a sentence, then ask what comes after theirs.

line: What's next for your team once this project is done?
followUps: Is that something you're looking forward to?
How did that end up on your plate?
shareBack: Mention what your own team turns to next, briefly, then ask what they'd choose if it were up to them.

line: That was a clear presentation. The example in the middle really landed. How did you come up with it?
followUps: How long did it take to get it that tight?
What did you cut that you wish you'd kept?
shareBack: Say which point you'll use yourself and how, then ask what they'd change next time.
deliveryCue: Name the specific part you liked; it should be true.

line: Good to meet you today. I enjoyed hearing about what you're working on.
followUps: How did the rest of your day go?
Would you be up for a coffee sometime to hear more?
shareBack: If they reply, mention one thing they said that stuck with you, then leave the next step open.
deliveryCue: Send the same day. It needs no reply.

line: Saw this and thought of what you said in the meeting. No need to reply.
followUps: Does it match what you've been seeing?
Have you come across anything else good on this?
shareBack: If they reply, say in one line what you took from it, then ask what they think.
deliveryCue: Attach the article or link. Only send something they'd really want.

line: Heading out for coffee in ten. Want anything, or want to come along?
followUps: How's your morning been so far?
Do you have a favorite place nearby?
shareBack: On the walk, mention one thing from your morning, then ask about theirs.

line: Thanks for today. The way you explained that made it click for me. Did it go how you hoped?
followUps: What would you do differently next time?
What's the next step from your side?
shareBack: Say in one line what you'll do with what they explained, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Be specific about what helped. A yes-or-no reply is fine.

line: Are you in the office tomorrow? I'm in and would be glad of lunch company.
followUps: Is there somewhere you've been wanting to try?
What time suits you?
shareBack: At lunch, offer one thing about your week first, then ask what theirs has been like.

line: Hope the trip back was easy. It was good to see you this week.
followUps: Did you get home at a reasonable hour?
Is next week a quieter one for you?
shareBack: If they reply, mention one moment from the visit you enjoyed, then wish them a good weekend.
deliveryCue: Needs no reply; a thumbs-up is a fine answer.

line: It's been a while. I walked past the place where we had lunch and thought of you. Hope things are going well.
followUps: Would a quick coffee or call sometime suit you?
What's been keeping you busy lately?
shareBack: If they reply, give one line on what you've been up to, then ask an easy question about them.
deliveryCue: Swap in your own real reminder. Ask for nothing.

line: No need for a long reply. Just checking the first week has gone smoothly on your side.
followUps: Is there anything that would make next week easier?
Would a quick call be useful, or is a message fine?
shareBack: If they reply, share one thing you noticed going well from your side, then ask if they agree.
deliveryCue: Change "first week" to whatever just happened.

line: Congratulations on the launch. I saw the announcement and it looked great. Is the team getting a breather now?
followUps: Which part are you proudest of?
What comes next?
shareBack: Say which detail of it you liked most, in one line, then leave the conversation open.
deliveryCue: Change "launch" to their real news.

line: That meeting ran long. Did you manage to get any lunch?
followUps: Want to grab something quick now?
Is the rest of your afternoon any calmer?
shareBack: Say how your own lunch plans survived, in a line, then suggest a real one another day.

line: Looking forward to seeing you on Thursday. Is there anything you'd like me to bring or prepare?
followUps: Who else from your side will be there?
Would you like to get lunch after?
shareBack: Mention the one thing you're hoping to cover, in a line, then ask if that fits their plan.
deliveryCue: Change the day. A one-word reply is enough.

line: You seemed a little flat after that meeting. No need to reply. I'm around if you want to talk it over.
followUps: Do you want to talk it through, or would a distraction be better?
What would help most right now?
shareBack: If they open up, listen first; later, mention a time a meeting left you feeling the same.
deliveryCue: Only for someone you know well. Don't push for an answer.

line: What are you working on at the moment that you're actually enjoying?
followUps: What is it about that one that you like?
How did you end up with it?
shareBack: Name the piece of your own work you're enjoying most, in a sentence, then ask what they'd like more of.

line: What's something you've picked up this year that's made the job easier?
followUps: How did you come across that?
What were you doing before you found it?
shareBack: Offer one small trick or habit that helped you, then ask whether they've tried anything like it.

line: Your meetings always finish on time and still get somewhere. How do you do it?
followUps: What do you do when someone goes off track?
Did you learn that from someone, or work it out?
shareBack: Admit one thing you find hard about running meetings, then ask what they'd try in your place.
deliveryCue: Only say it if it's true of them.

line: I have a tricky email to write and you're good at these. How would you open it?
followUps: What would you leave out?
Has one of these ever gone badly for you?
shareBack: Say what you were planning to write, briefly, then ask what they'd change.
deliveryCue: Ask only when they have a few minutes.

line: Seems like that project has a lot of moving parts right now.
followUps: Which part is taking most of your attention?
Is any of it fun, or is it all juggling?
shareBack: Mention a time you had something similar on your plate, in a sentence, then ask what would help.
deliveryCue: Say it as an observation and wait.

line: What's been on your mind most this week, work or otherwise?
followUps: What's making that one stick?
Is it a good kind of busy or the other kind?
shareBack: Offer the one thing you keep coming back to this week, briefly, then return to theirs.
deliveryCue: Give them time; let them choose how much to say.

line: Is there anything you'd like to be doing more of at work next year?
followUps: What draws you to that?
What would need to change for it to happen?
shareBack: Name one thing you'd like more of yourself, in a sentence, then ask how you could help with theirs.

line: Do you see yourself staying on this path, or is something else starting to pull at you?
followUps: How long has that been on your mind?
What would the first small step look like?
shareBack: Share where you honestly stand on your own path, in a sentence or two, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: For a private moment. Listen; don't steer.

line: I was thinking about that project we nearly didn't finish. What do you remember most about it?
followUps: Would you do it the same way again?
What did you take from it that you still use?
shareBack: Offer the one moment you remember best, in a sentence, then ask if they saw it the same way.

line: What's the strangest job you had before this one?
followUps: What was the best part of it?
Did anything from it turn out to be useful here?
shareBack: Tell your own oddest job in one sentence, with one detail, then ask for the rest of their story.
deliveryCue: Best over food or a drink.

line: What do you like to do to switch off after a week like this one?
followUps: How did you get into that?
Do you get to do it as often as you'd like?
shareBack: Mention the one thing that helps you switch off, in a sentence, then ask what they'd recommend trying.

line: Since we have the drive: what's the best work trip you've ever been on?
followUps: What made that one so good?
Is there a place you'd go back to on your own time?
shareBack: Offer your own best or worst work trip in a sentence, then ask where they'd like to be sent next.

line: Looking back, is there a call you made here that you'd make differently now?
followUps: What do you know now that you didn't then?
Has it changed how you decide things?
shareBack: Share one decision of your own you'd revisit, briefly, then ask what they'd tell someone facing it.
deliveryCue: Private setting only. Listen; don't fix.

line: You've been here longer than I have. What do you wish someone had told you in your first year?
followUps: How did you find that out in the end?
Who helped you most back then?
shareBack: Mention one thing you're still figuring out here, then ask what they'd do in your position.

line: Last time you mentioned things were about to get busy. How did that turn out?
followUps: What was the hardest part of it?
Is it settling down now?
shareBack: Offer a short update on what you mentioned last time too, then ask what's next for them.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real thing they told you last time.

line: What's gone better than you expected this year?
followUps: What do you think made the difference?
Did it change your plans for next year?
shareBack: Name one thing that surprised you on the upside, in a sentence, then ask what they're hoping for next.

line: What are you most excited about for the team over the next few months?
followUps: What would make that go really well?
Where do you think we can help most?
shareBack: Mention the piece of upcoming work you're most looking forward to, in a sentence, then ask how it fits their plans.

line: I was curious how you landed on the new priorities. What tipped it for you?
followUps: What was the hardest thing to leave off the list?
How do you test a decision like that before you commit?
shareBack: Say which priority makes most sense from where you sit, then ask what they'd like your team to keep in mind.
deliveryCue: Sound curious, not challenging.

line: You've handled a lot of difficult conversations. Any advice for someone with one coming up?
followUps: What do you do in the first minute?
Is there one that taught you the most?
shareBack: Describe your upcoming conversation in a sentence, without names, then ask what they'd watch for.

line: I enjoyed your talk earlier, especially the story at the start. How do you prepare for those?
followUps: How do you decide what to leave out?
Does it get easier the more of them you do?
shareBack: Mention the one point you'll take back to your own work, then ask what they'd add with more time.
deliveryCue: Name the part you really liked.

line: What are you reading or listening to lately that's been worth the time?
followUps: What's the main thing you took from it?
How do you find the good ones?
shareBack: Name one thing you've read or heard recently and one idea from it, then ask if they've come across it.

line: What's something you learned early in your career that you still use?
followUps: Who did you learn that from?
When has it mattered most?
shareBack: Offer one lesson you've picked up recently, in a sentence, then ask if it matches their experience.

line: I'd like to get better at presenting to senior people. What do you notice in the ones who do it well?
followUps: What's the most common mistake you see?
How should I open if I only have five minutes?
shareBack: Mention one thing you already do when presenting, then ask whether they'd keep it or drop it.

line: What's the part of the job you enjoy most these days?
followUps: Has that changed over the years?
What would you like more time for?
shareBack: Name the part of your own work you enjoy most, in a sentence, then ask a follow-up about theirs.

line: It feels like the team has found its rhythm this quarter.
followUps: What do you think made the difference?
What would you like us to keep doing?
shareBack: Offer one specific thing you've noticed working better, then ask whether they see it the same way.
deliveryCue: Only say it if you believe it.

line: How did you first get into this field?
followUps: What kept you in it?
Was there a turning point along the way?
shareBack: Give your own route in, in one sentence with one detail, then ask what they'd tell someone starting now.

line: Do you get much chance to come to these, or is tonight a rare one?
followUps: What's the best one you've been to?
Who else should I make sure to meet while I'm here?
shareBack: Say how often you make it to events like this, in a sentence, then ask what they're hoping to get from it.

line: I'm looking for a good book on leading a team. Is there one you'd recommend?
followUps: What did you take from it?
Is there one you'd tell people to skip?
shareBack: Mention the last useful thing you read, in a sentence, then ask if it's worth your time to go further.

line: What do you pay attention to when you want to know how things are really going?
followUps: How did you learn to look for that?
What do people tend to miss?
shareBack: Say what you tend to watch in your own work, briefly, then ask what else you should be noticing.

line: I thought delaying the launch was the right call. What made you confident about it?
followUps: What would have changed your mind?
How did you bring everyone along?
shareBack: Say what the decision made easier for you, in a sentence, then ask what they're watching next.
deliveryCue: Swap in a real decision you agreed with.

line: I've been trying to block out time for focused work, with mixed results. How do you protect yours?
followUps: What do you say no to?
Has that changed as your role has grown?
shareBack: Add what has and hasn't worked for you, in a sentence, then ask which of their habits to try first.

line: Thanks for making time for this. I know this week is a packed one.
followUps: Does it ease up after this week?
What's the main thing on your plate right now?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you're hoping to get from the time, then ask what would be most useful to them.
deliveryCue: Say it warmly, then pause before the agenda.

line: Is this your first time in the city, or do you know it well?
followUps: What have you managed to see so far?
Is there anything you'd like to fit in before you leave?
shareBack: Suggest one place you like nearby, in a sentence, then ask what kind of thing they enjoy.
deliveryCue: Use when they have traveled to you.

line: I've heard good things about your team from everyone who's worked with them. What's the secret?
followUps: How did you build that?
What do you look for when someone new joins?
shareBack: Mention one specific thing you've seen their team do well, then ask how they keep it up.
deliveryCue: Only if you have really heard it.

line: You know this market far better than I do. What should I be reading to keep up?
followUps: What's changed most in the last year or two?
Who do you think gets it right?
shareBack: Say what you currently follow, in a sentence, then ask whether it's giving you the right picture.

line: Is there a local dish or a place I should try while I'm in town?
followUps: What do you order there?
Where would you take a visitor for one good meal?
shareBack: Mention the best thing you've eaten on the trip so far, then ask if they'd agree with the choice.
deliveryCue: Use when you are the visitor.

line: How did your company get started on this? I'd like to hear the story behind it.
followUps: What was the hardest part early on?
What surprised you most along the way?
shareBack: Say what first caught your attention about their work, in a sentence, then ask what's next for it.

line: It sounds like this has been a big year for your team.
followUps: What are you proudest of from it?
What made it possible?
shareBack: Mention the one piece of their year you noticed from outside, then ask what they're aiming at next.
deliveryCue: Say it as an observation and let them fill in the rest.
